messages:
Anna Lopez: Observed spike in preemptive shard handoffs causing cascade evictions during region maintenance window. Proposing a lightweight brokering layer in policy engine to mediate preemptive handoffs + admission.
Mike Chen: Can you sketch the brokering flow? sounds like an extra hop on critical path.
Anna Lopez: Idea = policy layer becomes 'polymorphic broker' — it can reply with one of: ALLOW, DEFER(with ETA), REJECT, or BROKERED_HANDOFF(token). Runtime treats DEFER/BROKERED as short-circuit but not immediate eviction.
Sree Hari: Key tradeoff: added latency for first-token of a request vs. fewer cascades and less thrash. We should quantify p95 increase vs. reduction in cold-cache evictions.
Jamie Park: Interface boundary question: should runtime call policy synchronously on every routed request, or only on handoff events? If every request, cost multiplies.
Anna Lopez: Plan: default = event-driven calls (on handoff intent / slot preempt), optional sync check for high-risk tenants. Keep hot path minimal.
Mike Chen: Operationally we need a fallback when policy-broker is unavailable. What does runtime do? immediate ALLOW? immediate REJECT?
Sree Hari: Fallback should be conservative: ALLOW for latency-critical customers, REJECT for overloaded best-effort. But we need tenant-level policy. Suggest return of 'FALLBACK_HINT' in config.
Jamie Park: For config shape, propose:
```
policy_decision_request: {
  tenant_id: string,
  route_id: string,
  intent: "handoff" | "new_req",
  load_snapshot: { cpu_pct, gpu_mem_pct, inflight_count }
}
policy_decision_response: {
  decision: "ALLOW" | "DEFER" | "REJECT" | "BROKERED",
  eta_seconds?: number,
  broker_token?: string,
  reason?: string
}
```
Anna Lopez: That contract keeps runtime changes small. DEFER + ETA lets the runtime queue a tiny buffer or retry after ETA. BROKERED issues a token that transfers state gracefully between shards.
Mike Chen: How do we ensure tokens are verifiable and don't permit stale handoffs? Need short TTL + signature. Also need mechanism to cancel token if target slot disappears.
Sree Hari: Agree. Tokens = signed JSON (kid + exp) with slot fingerprint. Add reconciliation endpoint for runtime to poll if token still valid.
Jamie Park: Testing strategy? We should have a sim-mode in policy-sim that can fast-forward maintenance windows and inject timing jitter to measure cascading failures.
Anna Lopez: Yes — migration steps: 1) add sim-mode in policy-sim + load tests, 2) opt-in per-tenant DEFER via console flag, 3) rollout default to non-critical tenants, 4) monitor eviction rate & p95.
policy-bot: Deploy Scheduler: canary policy-broker v0.1 queued for eng-runtime test cluster at 03:15 UTC :rocket:
Mike Chen: Metrics we need: handoff_attempts, handoff_deferred, handoff_brokered, failed_handoffs, avg_defer_eta, p95-first-token-latency-by-tenant. Add tags for region and tier.
Sree Hari: Telemetry: capture pre/post cache-hit rates to ensure DEFER doesn't degrade effective cache warmness. Also log the reason string for postmortem.
Anna Lopez: Security note — broker_token must be scoped and auditable. KMS sign + runtime verify. We'll add audit events for token issue/consume/cancel.
Jamie Park: One more boundary: who owns the retry logic for DEFER? runtime or policy-broker? I vote runtime — simpler to implement and avoids extra state.
Anna Lopez: Agreed. Runtime will schedule a retry at ETA. If token path (BROKERED) used, the broker marks transfer in its local state.
Mike Chen: Ok next actions: Anna to draft RFC with contract + metrics + sim plan. I'll prototype token format and TTL. Sree to add telemetry hooks in policy-sim. Jamie to draft runtime retry/backoff behavior.
Anna Lopez: I'll drop RFC link when ready and add a short checklist for rollout. Thanks all :thumbsup:
